conventions.convention: Inner products are linear in the first argument. The rank-one operator |u⟩⟨v| sends x to ⟨x,v⟩u.
The subsystem order is H_G ⊗ H_L, with gauge first. Tr_G contracts the first factor and preserves the displayed order of all residual factors, including a reference.
Ordinary recovery is decoded to H_L and equals the identity on the full logical operator space; this also implies equality with every finite reference.
The coefficient convention is PE_a*E_bP = C_ab P, and transformed errors are F_i = Σ_a E_a U_ai. For the constructed recovery, the cross-error output is C_ba X.
Subsystem correction permits changing the gauge state but preserves the logical/reference marginal for every joint density operator and every finite reference.
Unknown error supports require 2t < d; errors supported on one fixed known set S require |S| < d.

load_bearing.statement: For an isometry V with nonzero logical space and a finite Kraus channel, PE_a*E_bP = C_ab P implies a finite Kraus decoded recovery R with R ∘ N ∘ Ad_V = id. For this recovery, R(E_a V X V* E_b*) = C_ba X for every logical operator X.

For nonzero finite-dimensional H_G and H_L, a channel preserving the logical marginal of every density operator has every chosen Kraus operator of the form A_j ⊗ I, with Σ_j A_j* A_j = I. Conversely, such a family preserves that marginal, including every finite reference. The stated gauge-reset-and-encode map is a channel.

Unitary mixing F_i = Σ_a E_a U_ai preserves the operator-sum map and gives V*F_i*F_jV = δ_ij λ_i I with λ_i ≥ 0. Zero-eigenvalue restrictions vanish; positive-eigenvalue restrictions normalize to isometries with pairwise orthogonal ranges.
Every operator in a finite Kraus representation of the identity channel on a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space is a scalar multiple of the identity.
Complex-linear maps between finite-dimensional operator spaces that agree on every unit-vector rank-one projector agree on all operators and after tensoring with the identity on any finite reference.

The protected subsystem is exactly correctable under J if and only if J*E_a*E_bJ = M_ab ⊗ I for every a,b. This is equivalent to the stated physical compression identities and embedded gauge matrix-unit identities.

Orthogonal complements and the rank-one positivity arguments.

concerns.concern: Verification step 2.1 writes the operator-valued table (V*E_a*E_bV)_{a,b} equal to the scalar matrix C. Here H_L = C², so its entries are actually C_ab I₂. The intended scalar-compression calculation is correct, but the displayed equality needs either the identity factors or an explicit scalar-identity identification.

Verification step 2.1 equates the operator-valued table (V*E_a*E_bV)_{a,b} with the scalar matrix diag(1/2,1/2). Its diagonal entries are (1/2)I₂. State the scalar-identity identification or display those identity factors.

alerts.finding: In thm-qc-stabilizer-distance-detection-and-correction, step 2.1 says: “The Knill–Laflamme theorem [F5] yields an exact recovery for this finite Pauli error family.” The cited thm-qc-knill-laflamme-explicit-recovery assumes that its error operators are Kraus operators of a trace-preserving channel. A family of M unscaled Pauli unitaries has adjoint-square sum M I, rather than I when M > 1. The proof has not normalized that family before this application. Uniform normalization supplies a channel, after which the constructed recovery or its cross-error formula gives the intended simultaneous correction.

seams_checked.note: Finite Kraus existence, complete positivity, normalization, and channel composition are used with their finite-dimensional hypotheses. Trace preservation is consistently required on the full operator space.

The encoding-projector identities and support conventions match. The distance supplier is used only for scalar compression below d; recovery is separately obtained from the local Knill–Laflamme theorem.
The first-factor trace is obtained by swapping before the supplier's second-factor trace. Tensor order, adjoints, product bases, zero-dimensional cases, and reference reassociation agree.

The F5/F8 quotations in the stabilizer and CSS results faithfully state the channel hypothesis. The stabilizer theorem's step 2.1 applies the supplier directly to an unnormalized Pauli family; the short normalization gap is recorded in alerts. Its final application to the stated channel and the CSS application retain the required hypotheses.

The deviation and gadget definitions use decoded recovery with finite references. The encoded-instrument lemma explicitly starts from a normalized mixed Pauli channel and derives transfer to encoded instruments, distinguishing those instruments from full-space CPTP errors and auxiliary memory from an untouched reference.
